name: Point Charge in Three Dimensions
description: The static spacetime of a point electric charge in two dimensions of space and one of time, whose field fills the plane and curves spacetime everywhere, with a horizon on the circle $r = r_c$ beyond which $r$ is a time.
convention:

u}F_{\alpha eta}F^{\alpha eta})/2\pi$ of the charge's field $F = (Q/r)\,dr \wedge c\,dt$, whose strength is $E = Q/r$.
history: Spread over a plane, the electric field of a point charge $Q$ weakens only as $E = Q/r$, so slowly that its total energy is infinite [gott1986charged, deser1985]. With two dimensions of space and no cosmological constant, Einstein's equations leave spacetime flat wherever there is no matter, and the field of the charge is matter at every radius, so it curves the whole of spacetime [gott1986charged, cataldo1996]. The static, circularly symmetric spacetime of the charge has the line element $ds^2 = -\dfrac{kQ^2}{2\pi}\ln\left(\dfrac{r_c}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{2\pi\,dr^2}{kQ^2\ln\left(\dfrac{r_c}{r}\right)} + r^2d\phi^2$, in which $r_c$ is a constant length and the circle of radius $r$ has circumference $2\pi r$ [gott1986charged, cataldo1996]. Here $k = 8\pi G/c^4$ couples matter to curvature, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions. The Ricci scalar, $R = kQ^2/2\pi r^2$, grows without bound at the charge. ¶ J. Richard Gott III and Mark Alpert found in 1984 that a point mass in three dimensions sits at the apex of a cone whose angle deficit is proportional to the mass [gott1984]. Stanley Deser and Pawel O. Mazur published the spacetime of a massive point charge in May 1985 [deser1985]. M. A. Melvin derived the electrostatic and magnetostatic solutions without a cosmological constant in January 1986, and J. Richard Gott III, Jonathan Z. Simon, and Mark Alpert published their electrically charged solution that October [garcia2009, melvin1986, gott1986charged]. Steven Carlip counts the three as independent discoveries of one metric [carlip1995]. Deser and Mazur found that the charge vanishes if the mechanical mass of the particle is large enough to close space, and that no static solution holds two or more charges [deser1985]. ¶ On the circle $r = r_c$ the logarithm vanishes and the spacetime has a horizon, which Gott, Simon, and Alpert likened to the inner horizon of the Reissner-Nordström black hole [gott1986charged]. Inside it the spacetime is static; outside it $r$ is a time [gott1986charged]. In their Kruskal extension, two static regions, each with a charge at $r = 0$, meet two dynamical ones [gott1986charged]. A spacelike slice across both static regions is "a football-shaped universe" with charge $Q$ at one end and $-Q$ at the other, and in the dynamical regions space is a cylinder, expanding in one and contracting in the other [gott1986charged]. For Deser and Mazur the circle is a Killing horizon, and the spacetime has no event horizon [deser1985]. ¶ Gott, Simon, and Alpert turned to Kaluza-Klein theory, in which electromagnetic radiation in three dimensions is gravitational radiation in four [gott1986charged]. In the same way, gravity in three dimensions carries no waves, and so electromagnetism in one dimension of space and one of time carries none [gott1986charged]. Benni Reznik investigated the thermodynamics of the charged horizon in 1992 [reznik1992]. Ian I. Kogan used proper radial distance to describe the electric solution in 1992, including geometries with either sign of the gravitational coupling [kogan1992]. Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli gave their black hole of 1992 an electric charge, and with the cosmological constant set to zero the static charged solution is this metric [banados1992, carlip1995]. ¶ Peter Peldán derived the circularly symmetric electrostatic family with a cosmological constant in 1993 and recovered this spacetime when that constant vanishes [peldan1993]. François Englert and Reznik derived the entropy of the charged horizon from semiclassical tunneling in 1994 for a smooth charged source [tunneling1994]. The entropy is proportional to the horizon circumference [tunneling1994]. In two dimensions of space the electric field is a vector and the magnetic field a scalar, so Hodge duality does not exchange them [cataldo1996]. Mauricio Cataldo and Patricio Salgado showed in 1996 that a magnetic solution follows from the static charged spacetime of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli by exchanging the time with the angle and the electric charge with the magnetic one, each with a factor of $i$ [cataldo1996]. Gérard Clément generated a spinning charged family from the static charged spacetime with a negative cosmological constant in 1996 [clement1996]. ¶ Cristián Martínez, Teitelboim, and Zanelli derived the charged rotating geometry by boosting the static solution in 2000 [mtz2000]. The boost mixes time with the periodic angle, so the static and rotating spacetimes can have different global identifications [mtz2000, maeda2024]. Martínez and coauthors defined the mass relative to a reference radius, absorbing the divergent electric energy into the mass parameter [mtz2000]. Daisuke Ida proved in 2000 that matter obeying the dominant energy condition forbids a black hole in three dimensions with a positive cosmological constant, and noted that with no cosmological constant a Maxwell field rules out even degenerate apparent horizons [ida2000blackhole]. Alberto A. García classified stationary, circularly symmetric Einstein-Maxwell geometries in 2009 and related the static electric solution to the rotating families through transformations of time and angle [garcia2009]. García tabulated the energy and Cotton tensor eigenvectors of the stationary families in a 2013 preprint [garcia2013]. ¶ Glenn Barnich, Pierre-Henry Lambert, and Pujian Mao included the static charged spacetime in a family with asymptotically flat boundary conditions at null infinity in 2015 [barnich2015]. The algebra of conserved charges contains a term depending on the electric charge [barnich2015]. Dionisios Sotirios Krongos and Charles G. Torre derived the static charged family from conditions on the curvature alone in 2017 [rainich2017]. The metric determines the electromagnetic field up to its sign [rainich2017]. Chethan Krishnan and coauthors constructed charged boson stars inside a circular cavity with no cosmological constant in 2020 [hairybox2020]. The stars contain a massless charged scalar field and have a regular centre [hairybox2020]. ¶ Jiří Podolský and Matúš Papajčík classified local Einstein-Maxwell geometries with no charges or currents and any cosmological constant in 2022 [podolsky2022]. The geometries separate into a nonexpanding Kundt class and an expanding Robinson-Trautman class [podolsky2022]. The static spacetime of the charge belongs to the expanding class [podolsky2022]. Podolský and Papajčík classified its Cotton tensor in 2023: it is type I away from the horizon and type III on the horizon [cotton2023]. ¶ Hideki Maeda and Podolský constructed coordinates that extend across the horizon of the charged rotating family in 2024 [maeda2024]. For the static spacetime, their time coordinate is the proper time of a family of radially falling observers [maeda2024]. Pujian Mao and Weicheng Zhao showed in 2024 that the horizon is cosmological, with every circle beyond $r_c$ trapped [mao2024]. With no cosmological constant, Mao and Zhao related the rotating family locally to the static spacetime by a change of coordinates [mao2024]. Jorrit Bosma, Marc Geiller, Sucheta Majumdar, and Blagoje Oblak included both Coulomb fields and electromagnetic radiation in the asymptotically flat family in 2024 [radiative2024]. The Bondi mass decreases as electromagnetic radiation escapes through null infinity [radiative2024]. ¶ Shoichiro Miyashita studied the thermodynamics of this geometry with a circular boundary and no cosmological constant in 2024 [miyashita2024]. The horizon circumference exceeds the circumference of the boundary, and the Euclidean time circle closes smoothly at the horizon [miyashita2024, miyashita2025]. At fixed boundary radius and chemical potential, the entropy is independent of temperature and the heat capacity vanishes at leading order in the gravitational path integral [miyashita2024, miyashita2025]. Miyashita added a charged scalar field in 2025 and found thermal geometries with scalar hair [miyashita2025]. With scalar hair, the horizon size can change with temperature at fixed chemical potential [miyashita2025].

related.text: A mass in three dimensions leaves space flat around it, a cone with its tip at the mass [gott1984]. Give the particle a charge, and its field, spread over the plane, curves spacetime everywhere [gott1986charged].
Give the black hole of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli an electric charge and set its cosmological constant to zero, and it becomes this spacetime [banados1992, carlip1995].
The Reissner-Nordström black hole keeps its charge inside two horizons. Gott, Simon, and Alpert likened the one horizon at $r_c$ to the inner of the two [gott1986charged].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Coupling of Einstein's equations, $k = 8\pi G/c^4$ with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Electric charge of the source at $r = 0$
Radius of the horizon, a constant of integration independent of $Q$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $2\pi r$ the circumference of the circle of radius $r$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Coupling of Einstein's equations, $k = 8\pi G/c^4$ with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Electric charge of the source at $r = 0$
Radius of the horizon, a constant of integration independent of $Q$

coordinates.convention: We use Podolský and Papajčík's coordinates $(u, r, \phi)$, with $u$ the retarded time, $c\,du = c\,dt - 2\pi\,dr/(kQ^2\ln(r_c/r))$, constant along every outgoing light ray. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cu$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{u}$ means $d(cu)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Coupling of Einstein's equations, $k = 8\pi G/c^4$ with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Electric charge of the source at $r = 0$
Radius of the horizon, a constant of integration independent of $Q$

coordinates.convention: We use Mao and Zhao's coordinates $(v, r, \phi)$, with $v$ the advanced time, $c\,dv = c\,dt + 2\pi\,dr/(kQ^2\ln(r_c/r))$, constant along every ingoing light ray. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cv$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{v}$ means $d(cv)/d\lambda$.
